pages.note: The chant continuing; no heading. TWO SETTINGS ON ONE SHEET: eighteen TWO-COLUMN rows (gutter measured at 251px, x 801-1051), then a SINGLE-COLUMN centred block of eight lines at the foot (profiled separately; no interior corridor). The two-column part finishes the Four Great Kings, names their crafty servants and the gandhabba companies, then the nāga hosts; the foot block turns to the supaṇṇas and their peace with the nāgas.

checks.issue: THE SHEET CHANGES SETTING PART WAY DOWN. Rows 1-18 are set in TWO COLUMNS, one gāthā-half to each column, so a verse is one ROW read left then right — the same unit as pages 176-178. The last eight lines are set SINGLE COLUMN and centred, one pāda to a line, because they are in the longer tuṭṭhubha metre. Both blocks were ink-profiled separately: the two-column band has a clear 251px corridor at x 801-1051, the foot band has none. The verse unit therefore changes from a row to a line at verse 87, which is the book's own layout and not a fault. The same split was handled the same way at verses 12-15 on page 176.

⚠ วิรุพหะโก IS PRINTED WITH พ, not ฬ. He is Virūḷhaka, Great King of the South, and both the canon and the roman twin have ḷ — twin verse 96 reads `Purimadisaṃ dhataraṭṭho, dakkhiṇena viruḷhako`. ⚠ NOTE ALSO that page 178's own batch note asserted `page 179 gives วิรุฬหะโก`; the photograph does NOT bear that out — this sheet gives พ. Read from a 4.2× crop and confirmed a second time against the neighbouring rows. Entered as this page prints it, romanised `virubhako` by the same พ→b rule already used for วิรุพโห→virubho and ทัพเหนะ→dabhena. The LONG ending -ako that 178 predicted IS correct; only the consonant differs.

⚠ นะโพราชา IS PRINTED WITH พ, not ฬ — the second ฬ→พ failure on this one sheet. He is Naḷa, and the roman twin verse 104 reads `Cittaseno ca gandhabbo naḷo rājā janosabho`. Read from a 4.2× crop; the glyph has no ascender and is identical in shape to the พ of คันธัพโพ earlier in the same row, while this same printing DOES set ฬ correctly at verse 56 on page 178 (วิรุฬโห). The glyph is available to the printer, so this is a setting failure and not a house convention. Entered as printed, romanised `nabo rājā`. The twin corroborates ชะโนสะโภ → janosabho.

⚠ สะมิตัง IS PRINTED WITH ั HERE where verses 70 and 86 on this SAME SHEET print สะมิติง, and where every earlier occurrence of the refrain (verses 35, 38, 41, 44, 47, 55, 60, 65) has สะมิติง. The roman twin verse 107 has `samitiṃ`. Read at 5× against the วะนัง of its own line, whose ั is the same shape, and against the สะมิติง of rows 2 and 18. The difference is real and on the page. Entered as printed, `samitaṃ`; not normalised to its neighbours.

⚠ สัญหาหิ IS PRINTED WITH ญ where the roman twin verse 118 has `Saṇhāhi` with ṇ, and it carries NO cluster mark at all — where ṇh would want one. Read at 5× and compared glyph-for-glyph with the ณ of สุปัณณา one line below: the ณ sits on the baseline with small feet, while this glyph hangs a full descender loop below it. It is ญ. Entered as printed, `sañhāhi`.

A DIFFERENCE FROM THE TWIN. This sheet sets วิฏู จะ วิฏุโต — long ู on the first, and a PLAIN ต closing the second, checked at 5× against the ฏ earlier in the same word, which carries the loop this one lacks. The roman copy sets `viṭuca viṭuṭo`: short u, the two words run together, and a retroflex ṭ at the end. Entered as this page prints it, `viṭū ca viṭuto`.
A DIFFERENCE FROM THE TWIN. This sheet sets สุริยะวัจฉะสา, giving `suriyavacchasā` with จฉ = cch; the roman copy sets `suriyavaccasā` with cc. Entered as this page prints it.

A DIFFERENCE FROM THE TWIN. This sheet sets สะระณะมะกังสุ with ก, giving `saraṇamakaṃsu`; the roman copy sets `saraṇa-magaṃsu` with g. Here the THAI sheet agrees with the canon — akaṃsu is the aorist of karoti — so the twin is the copy at fault. Entered as this page prints it; the twin has not been touched.

A WORD-DIVISION DIFFERENCE FROM THE TWIN, letters identical. This sheet sets สะหะตัจฉะกา as one word, giving `sahatacchakā`; the roman copy sets `saha tacchakā` as two. Entered as this page prints it.

THE CLUSTER MARK ON THIS SHEET IS THANTHAKHAT ์, NOT YAMAKKAN ๎ — จิต์รา at verse 90 and อุปะว์หะยันตา at verse 93. Checked at 5× against the ั of อะภะยันตะทา one line above: the ั is a plain small hook, while these marks carry the loop and rising tail of ์. That matches the rest of this chant, which sets ์ throughout (กะปิละวัตถุส์มิง, อุปะสังกะมิต์วา, ปะวะนัส์มิง, ตัต์ระ), so the chant is internally consistent.

THE SHEET OPENS MID-GROUP. Verses 69 and 70 complete Kuvera's sons, counted in the last row of 178; the page turn falls between the count and its two closing lines, exactly as it did between 177 and 178.

อาคู IS SET WITH A LONG ู throughout this sheet — verses 75, 80, 83, 84 and 85. The roman twin agrees, reading `āgū` at each. This is the first time the word enters the app, so the long ū is the precedent it sets.

ROWS 3 AND 15 ARE INDENTED on the sheet, marking the start of a new group — the Four Great Kings named together at row 3, and the nāga hosts at row 15. The indent is the book's paragraphing; it carries no label, so nothing has been added to the page blocks for it.

verses.pali: อิทธิมันโต ชุติมันโต วัณณะวันโต ยะสัสสิโน
verses.english: possessed of power, of radiance, of beauty and of renown,

verses.pali: โมทะมานา อะภิกกามุง ภิกขูนัง สะมิติง วะนัง.
verses.english: came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.

verses.pali: ปุริมะทิสัง ธะตะรัฏโฐ ทักขิเณนะ วิรุพหะโก
verses.english: Dhataraṭṭha to the eastern quarter, Viruḷhaka to the south,

verses.pali: ปัจฉิเมนะ วิรูปักโข กุเวโร อุตตะรัง ทิสัง.
verses.english: Virūpakkha to the west, and Kuvera to the northern quarter.

verses.pali: จัตตาโร เต มะหาราชา สะมันตา จะตุโร ทิสา
verses.pali_roman: Cattāro te mahārājā samantā caturo disā
verses.english: These four great kings, on every side, in the four directions,

verses.pali: ทัททัลละมานา อัฏฐังสุ วะเน กาปิละวัตถะเว.
verses.english: stood there blazing, in the wood at Kapilavatthu.

verses.pali: เตสัง มายาวิโน ทาสา อาคู วัญจะนิกา สะฐา
verses.pali_roman: Tesaṃ māyāvino dāsā āgū vañcanikā saṭhā
verses.english: Their conjuring servants came too, deceivers and tricksters:

verses.pali: มายา กุเฏณฑุ เวเฏณฑุ วิฏู จะ วิฏุโต สะหะ.
verses.pali_roman: Māyā kuṭeṇḍu veṭeṇḍu viṭū ca viṭuto saha.
verses.english: Māyā, Kuṭeṇḍu and Veṭeṇḍu, Viṭū and Viṭuta with them.

verses.pali: จันทะโน กามะเสฏโฐ จะ กินนุฆัณฑุ นิฆัณฑุ จะ
verses.pali_roman: Candano kāmaseṭṭho ca kinnughaṇḍu nighaṇḍu ca
verses.english: Candana and Kāmaseṭṭha, Kinnughaṇḍu and Nighaṇḍu,

verses.pali: ปะนาโท โอปะมัญโญ จะ เทวะสูโต จะ มาตะลิ.
verses.pali_roman: Panādo opamañño ca devasūto ca mātali.
verses.english: Panāda and Opamañña, and Mātali the charioteer of the devas.

verses.pali: จิตตะเสโน จะ คันธัพโพ นะโพราชา ชะโนสะโภ
verses.pali_roman: Cittaseno ca gandhabbo nabo rājā janosabho
verses.english: Cittasena the gandhabba, Naḷa the king, and Janosabha,

verses.pali: อาคู ปัญจะสิโข เจวะ ติมพะรู สุริยะวัจฉะสา.
verses.english: Pañcasikha came, and Timbarū, and Suriyavacchasā.

verses.pali: เอเต จัญเญ จะ ราชาโน คันธัพพา สะหะ ราชุภิ
verses.pali_roman: Ete caññe ca rājāno gandhabbā saha rājubhi
verses.english: These and other kings, gandhabbas together with their rulers,

verses.pali: โมทะมานา อะภิกกามุง ภิกขูนัง สะมิตัง วะนัง.
verses.english: came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.

verses.pali: อะถาคู นาภะสา นาคา เวสาลา สะหะตัจฉะกา
verses.english: Then came the nāgas of Nābhasa, and those of Vesālī with the Tacchakas,

verses.pali: กัมพะลัสสะตะรา อาคู ปายาคา สะหะ ญาติภิ.
verses.english: the Kambalas and Assataras came, and those of Payāga with their kin.

verses.pali: ยามูนา ธะตะรัฏฐา จะ อาคู นาคา ยะสัสสิโน
verses.pali_roman: Yāmūnā dhataraṭṭhā ca āgū nāgā yasassino
verses.english: The nāgas of the Yamunā and of Dhataraṭṭha's line came too, nāgas of renown,

verses.pali: เอราวัณโณ มะหานาโค โสปาคะ สะมิติง วะนัง.
verses.english: and Erāvaṇa the great nāga — he too came to the wood, to the assembly.

verses.pali: เย นาคะราเช สะหะสา หะรันติ
verses.english: Those who carry off the nāga kings by force,

verses.pali: ทิพพา ทิชา ปักขิ วิสุทธะจักขู
verses.english: divine twice-born winged ones, of pure sight —

verses.pali: เวหายะสา เต วะนะมัชฌะปัตตา
verses.english: through the air they came, and reached the middle of the wood:

verses.pali: จิต์รา สุปัณณา อิติ เตสะนามัง.
verses.english: Citrā and Supaṇṇā, these are their names.

verses.pali: อะภะยันตะทา นาคะราชานะมาสิ
verses.english: But the nāga kings were made fearless then,

verses.pali: สุปัณณะโต เขมะมะกาสิ พุทโธ
verses.english: for the Buddha made them safe from the supaṇṇas;

verses.pali: สัญหาหิ วาจาหิ อุปะว์หะยันตา
verses.english: and calling upon one another with gentle words,

verses.pali: นาคา สุปัณณา สะระณะมะกังสุ พุทธัง.
verses.english: nāgas and supaṇṇas took the Buddha as their refuge.

batch_status.pali_untouched: Typed from MAGNIFIED crops of this sheet — both columns in halves at 2.6×, the foot block at 2.0×, and eight further crops at 4.2×-8× for the contested glyphs — and then compared line by line with the roman twin at verses 94-119.
batch_status.page_scan: agrees. Two blocks, twenty-six verses: eighteen two-column rows then eight single-column lines.
batch_status.notes: Page 179: the servants of the Great Kings, the gandhabbas, the nāga hosts, and the supaṇṇas making peace. ⚠ TWO ฬ→พ FAILURES ON ONE SHEET — วิรุพหะโก at verse 71 and นะโพราชา at verse 79 — against a printing that sets ฬ correctly at verse 56 on page 178, so the glyph is available and this is a setting fault. ⚠ Page 178's batch note predicted วิรุฬหะโก here; the photograph shows พ, and the note is wrong on the consonant though right on the long -ako ending. ⚠ สะมิตัง at verse 82 against สะมิติง at 70 and 86 on this same sheet. ⚠ สัญหาหิ at verse 93 with ญ where the twin has ṇ. Nothing normalised. The sheet also changes setting part way down, two columns to one, and the verse unit changes with it.
